defects.title: Suspension is not enforced on existing sessions, and a banned user can erase their own ban via DELETE /me
defects.claim: authenticate() in server/src/db.ts:129-147 selects only `user_id, last_used` from `sessions` and never looks at `users.banned_at`. The only ban checks are at index.ts:198 (new sign-ins) and links.ts:182 (`createShare`). `live()` at links.ts:139-144 does not consider whether the share owner is banned, and `putPoster` has no ban check. `deleteAccount` at index.ts:383-391 runs `DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?`, which removes `banned_at` along with the row, so the next Discord login creates a fresh account through `upsertDiscordUser`. `closeAll(reason)` at hub.ts:178 is only ever called from `deleteAccount`; there are no admin/moderation HTTP endpoints (moderation is done by hand with `wrangler d1 execute`), so nothing runs `Hub.closeAll` or deletes sessions when someone is suspended. A suspended user keeps a working session, presence, relays, friend requests, live share links/media and poster swaps; only `POST /shares` is refused.
defects.scenario: Repro with seeded user C (`banned_at` set, live session): `GET /me` -> 200; WebSocket hello -> C's presence ('Banned Game') reached friend A; a relay from C was delivered to A. On banned user B: the existing share page and media still return 200 and `PUT /shares/:id/poster` -> 200; only `POST /shares` -> 403. `DELETE /me` by C -> 200 and the users row (including `banned_at`) is gone. Scenario: someone shares abusive clips and the operator sets `banned_at`; their 180-day session keeps working, they keep using presence, sending clips to friends and sending friend requests, their live links stay up and they can swap a link's poster (the `og:image` Discord embeds show) to any JPEG; then they run `DELETE /me`, sign in again with the same Discord account and get a clean account with fresh quota. Capability needed: a suspended user who still holds a token (the normal case, because nothing deletes sessions on suspension).
defects.fix: In db.ts authenticate: `SELECT s.user_id, s.last_used, u.banned_at FROM sessions s JOIN users u ON u.id = s.user_id WHERE s.token_hash = ?`; `if (!s || now - s.last_used > SESSION_IDLE_MS) throw new HttpError(401, ...)`; `if (s.banned_at !== null) throw new HttpError(403, "This account is suspended.")`. In links.ts live(): `... FROM shares s JOIN users u ON u.id = s.owner WHERE s.id = ? AND u.banned_at IS NULL`. Keep bans outside `users` (a `banned_discord_ids` table checked in `authCallback` before the upsert), or refuse `DELETE /me` while banned, or keep a minimal row. Add a cron 'suspension apply' step: find users with `banned_at` set and `suspended_applied_at IS NULL`, delete their sessions, take down their shares (R2 + tombstone), and call `HUB.getByName(id).closeAll("suspended")` (avoids a new admin HTTP surface). Also check the ban in `putPoster`.

defects.title: POST /t/ping is unauthenticated and unthrottled; each fresh-UUID ping writes ~6 D1 rows kept 400 days, exhausting the shared daily write quota
defects.claim: `POST /t/ping` (telemetry.ts:83-111) has no rate limit; the only check is the body shape. Each ping with a fresh random UUIDv4 inserts into `installs` and `install_days`; counting their PK and secondary indexes, that is roughly 6 D1 'rows written' per request, and the rows are kept 400 days. The D1 database and its Free-plan daily limits (about 100k rows written, 5M rows read) are shared by the whole app.
defects.scenario: A script sends ~20k pings per day (about one every 4 s) and exhausts the free D1 write allowance. After that every D1 write fails until 00:00 UTC: sign-in, `sessions.last_used` touches, uploads and friend actions. On a paid plan, unbounded growth and billing take the place of the outage. No capability is needed. Confirmed in code; the platform limits (Free plan inferred from code comments) are a 'likely' assumption. Severity: High on Free plan, Medium on paid.
defects.fix: Add a rate-limit binding `PING_LIMIT` keyed by `CF-Connecting-IP` (for example 5/60 s), as `REPORT_LIMIT` already does without storing the address. Turn off `workers_dev`, or WAF rules can be bypassed through it. Optionally drop pings whose `version` is not a known release.

defects.title: GET /auth/start is unthrottled and runs a full-table DELETE on logins (no created_at index), so D1 reads grow quadratically
defects.claim: Each unauthenticated `GET /auth/start` (index.ts:139-143) runs `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?`, and `logins` has no index on `created_at`, so every request scans the whole table. It then runs an INSERT that touches the table plus 2 unique indexes. There is no rate limit. R requests inside 10 minutes cost about R^2/2 rows read.
defects.scenario: 3,000 requests inside 10 minutes cost about 4.5M rows read, which is close to the whole Free-plan daily D1 read allowance (5M) shared by the entire app. No capability is needed. Severity: High on Free plan, Medium on paid.
defects.fix: Add an `AUTH_LIMIT` rate-limit binding keyed by `CF-Connecting-IP`. `CREATE INDEX logins_created ON logins(created_at)`, and move the logins cleanup into the cron. Turn off `workers_dev` so WAF rules cannot be bypassed.

defects.title: Site proxy GET /get/<ref> lets any browser-UA client add D1 writes to the shared database, with unbounded new refs kept 400 days
defects.claim: In the site proxy, `/get[/ref]` (site-proxy/index.ts:67-75) adds +1 to `downloads(day, ref)` in the same D1 database whenever the request is a GET from a non-bot User-Agent, with no rate limit. `ref` is any `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`, so every new ref creates a row kept 400 days. The count happens even if the client aborts right after the headers.
defects.scenario: Any client with a browser User-Agent repeatedly requests `/get/<new-ref>`, adding D1 writes to the database shared with the friends Worker (contributing to the app-wide daily write-quota outage) and creating 400-day rows; download counts can be forged freely. Severity: High on Free plan, Medium on paid.
defects.fix: Add a rate-limit binding or a WAF rule for `/get` in the site proxy; optionally cap distinct refs per day.

defects.title: Hourly sweepUsage does a full scan of installs because installs.last_day has no index
defects.claim: The hourly cron `sweepUsage` (telemetry.ts:119) runs `DELETE FROM installs WHERE last_day < ?`. `installs.last_day` has no index, so this is a full table scan every hour (rows read = install count x 24 per day). Fake pings via the unthrottled `/t/ping` inflate it further.
defects.scenario: As `installs` grows (including from fake pings), the hourly full scans consume an increasing share of the Free-plan daily D1 rows-read allowance shared by the whole app. Reported under the 'High on Free plan, Medium on paid' D1-quota finding.
defects.fix: `CREATE INDEX installs_last_day ON installs(last_day)`, and run `sweepUsage` once a day.

defects.title: Hub Durable Object: unlimited sockets per user, no rate limit on hello/presence, relay budget is per connection
defects.claim: `acceptWebSocket` at hub.ts:66 has no cap on sockets per user. The relay budget (intended 30 per 10 s) lives in `this.relayed`, keyed per WebSocket (hub.ts:248-252), so more sockets multiply it. Every `hello` or `presence` message (hub.ts:89-98) runs `sendSnapshot`, then `publish`: a Durable Object storage write, a D1 `friendIds` query, and one RPC to each friend's Hub, which in turn sends to every one of that friend's sockets; there is no rate limit on these messages. Every relay does a D1 `areFriends` lookup (hub.ts:256), even when the result is 'not a friend'.
defects.scenario: Repro: 4 sockets of one user delivered 119 relays in about 2 s (intended limit 30 per 10 s); 200 presence flips produced 200 fan-out messages at a friend. One free Discord account opens N sockets and spams relays to random UUIDs, or flips its presence; every message costs a D1 read and Durable Object requests or storage writes, draining the account-wide D1 and Durable Object daily quotas for everyone and flooding friends' apps.
defects.fix: Cap sockets per user (e.g. close the oldest beyond 5). Apply one per-connection budget to all message types and close the socket with code 4008 on abuse. Keep the per-user relay budget in `ctx.storage` or in memory per user, not per socket. Cache the friend set in the Hub, invalidated by `friendsChanged`, so relays do not hit D1. Coalesce `publish` calls (debounce about 1 s).

defects.title: 'Appear offline' can be detected through a relay probe
defects.claim: `relay()` at hub.ts:158-162 delivers to every `ready` socket and returns true without checking `attachment.invisible`, so the sender only gets `relayFailed: "offline"` when the target has truly no sockets. An invisible user is therefore distinguishable from an offline one, contradicting the privacy page promise: "With 'Appear offline', friends see you as offline."
defects.scenario: Repro: B said hello with `invisible: true`; A relayed `{id: "probe"}`: there was no `relayFailed`, and B received the probe. Any accepted friend can poll a body that the target's app ignores and learn exactly when an invisible friend is online.
defects.fix: If `this.current() === null` (invisible or offline), do not deliver and answer "offline". Alternatively, have the app opt in per relay. Either way the answer must look the same.

defects.title: Unbounded request bodies are read into memory, including on unauthenticated routes
defects.claim: `body()` at util.ts:16-22 calls `request.json()` with no size limit; it is used by `/auth/exchange` (unauthenticated), `/me` PATCH and `/friends/request`. At telemetry.ts:85-87 the size check relies on Content-Length, which is absent in chunked uploads, then calls `request.text()`. links.ts:324 does `JSON.parse((await request.text()).slice(0, 2048))`, reading everything and then slicing. `putPoster` already guards against this (see its comment at links.ts:276), but these routes do not.
defects.scenario: Repro: a 5 MB chunked body to `/t/ping` was read completely before the 400 came back. Bodies of up to 100 MB (the edge limit) are buffered and decoded, which can exceed the isolate's 128 MB memory and kill other requests running on the same isolate. The report notes severity is Medium-Low in practice because the attacker pays the bandwidth.
defects.fix: A shared `readLimited(request, max)` that streams with `getReader()`, cancels and returns 413 once `max` is passed, and rejects when Content-Length exceeds `max`. Validate that the parsed JSON is an object (this also fixes the null-body 500).

defects.title: A few throwaway accounts can keep the global share bucket 'full' with abandoned pending uploads
defects.claim: shares.ts:18 sets `TOTAL_BYTES = 9 GB` with `WEEKLY_LIMIT = 3` per account. At links.ts:57 a pending upload holds its declared `bytes` for up to 30 minutes, and an aborted upload is deleted (links.ts:252), so it does not use up a weekly slot. Reservations can be re-opened repeatedly at no quota cost.
defects.scenario: About 60 Discord accounts each keep 3 x 50 MB uploads open with a stalled body. Every 30 minutes the reservations lapse and the attacker simply re-opens them. Everyone else gets 507 'Sharing is full' indefinitely, and almost nothing is stored. Real 50 MB uploads from the same accounts do it for 5 days at a time. Likely.
defects.fix: Count a pending reservation against the week even after it is abandoned (keep the row with `aborted = 1` instead of deleting it). Cap how many bytes a single account can have live. Alert on a full bucket. Consider a per-IP rate limit on `POST /shares`.

defects.title: Share pages reveal the uploader's Discord user ID via the avatar URL
defects.claim: db.ts:88 builds the avatar URL as `https://cdn.discordapp.com/avatars/${user.id}/${hash}.png`, and page.ts:116 puts it into the public share page whenever `show_name` is set (the default, which users opt out of), exposing the Discord snowflake user ID. The privacy page only says 'display name and avatar'. Also, `show_name` is frozen at upload time, so turning the setting off later does not hide the name on links that are already live.
defects.scenario: Anyone who has the link can read the snowflake ID from the HTML and look up the exact Discord account.
defects.fix: Proxy the avatar through a route such as `/c/:id/avatar`, or use the default avatar, or disclose it.

defects.title: The e2e script seeds known bearer tokens into the production database
defects.claim: scripts/e2e.mjs:11-21 defaults `BASE` to the production workers.dev address and seeds fixed tokens `tok-a-test-only` / `tok-b-test-only` and friend codes `AAAAAAAA` / `BBBBBBBB`, all in a public repo. Cleanup relies on a comment ('Remove the accounts afterwards').
defects.scenario: If the seed is ever applied and not removed, anyone can act as those accounts, including uploading 3 public links per week each. Speculative as to the current state; check with `SELECT * FROM users WHERE discord_id LIKE 'test-%'`. Severity: Medium, if left seeded.
defects.fix: Generate random tokens at seed time and print them; default to a local `wrangler dev`; give the seeded rows a short `last_used` expiry or a cleanup cron.

defects.title: A 60-second Hub alarm per online user burns the Free-plan Durable Object request quota
defects.claim: The Hub arms a 60-second alarm per online user (hub.ts:33,76,135). Alarm invocations count as Durable Object requests: 1,440 per day for each always-online user.
defects.scenario: Against the Free-plan 100k Durable Object requests per day, that caps the service at roughly 70 always-online users, before counting presence RPCs. Severity: Medium on Free plan.
defects.fix: Sweep every 5 minutes, or skip re-arming when every socket was auto-pinged recently.

defects.title: Report handling: reports never surfaced, owner can destroy evidence, clips expire unreviewed, reports forgeable cross-site
defects.claim: (1) Reports filed via `POST /c/:id/report` are never surfaced to anyone; the operator has to poll D1. (2) The owner can delete a reported clip (`deleteShare` wipes it from R2 and blanks the title), which destroys the evidence. (3) Clips expire after 5 days whether or not anyone reviewed them. (4) Any website can make its visitors' browsers file reports (no-cors `text/plain` POST); the rate limit (`REPORT_LIMIT`, 5/min) is per IP and per Cloudflare location, and IPv6 rotation gets around it.
defects.scenario: An abusive clip is reported but nobody is notified; the owner deletes it (destroying the evidence) or it expires after 5 days unreviewed. A malicious website silently makes its visitors' browsers file reports, and IPv6 rotation bypasses the per-IP limit. Severity: Low-Medium.
defects.fix: Hide a clip automatically after N distinct-IP reports, notify the operator (webhook or email), and move reported objects to a quarantine prefix instead of deleting them.

defects.title: The download endpoint trusts release.setup.url without pinning it
defects.claim: site-proxy/index.ts:61 streams whatever URL `release.json` (read from Pages) names in `release.setup.url`, served as `ClippiBoy_<v>_x64-setup.<ref>.exe` from clippiboy.com, without validating the URL origin or the version format.
defects.scenario: Any compromise of the Pages content, the bake workflow, or the `einfabo` GitHub namespace makes the official domain serve an arbitrary binary. Severity: Low-Medium.
defects.fix: Require `setup.url` to start with `https://github.com/EinFabo/clippiboy/releases/download/` and `version` to match `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`.

defects.title: A null or non-object JSON body gives a 500
defects.claim: `body()` at util.ts:16-22 casts the parsed JSON without validating that it is an object, and callers destructure the result (for example index.ts:212), so a `null` or non-object body throws and returns 500.
defects.scenario: Repro: `/auth/exchange` and `/me` PATCH with body `null` -> 500.
defects.fix: Have `body()` reject anything that is not an object; check `typeof code === "string"`.

defects.title: Two users sending each other friend requests at the same moment get a 500
defects.claim: In the friend-request handler (index.ts:326-342), both concurrent requests pass the `existing` check, and the second INSERT into `friendships` hits the (ordered pair) primary key, returning 500.
defects.scenario: A and B send each other friend requests simultaneously; one of them receives a 500 instead of the pair being accepted.
defects.fix: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(user_a, user_b) DO UPDATE SET status='accepted' WHERE requester <> excluded.requester`, then re-read the row.

defects.title: Presence can arrive at friends out of order
defects.claim: `publish` at hub.ts:219-237 awaits D1 and RPCs, which opens the Durable Object's input gate, so two quick hello/presence messages can interleave. Friends may receive the older presence last and keep showing it.
defects.scenario: A user changes presence twice in quick succession; the two publishes interleave and friends end up displaying the stale first presence. Likely.
defects.fix: Add a sequence number or `at` to `friendPresence` and have receivers drop older ones; or serialize `publish` through a promise chain.

defects.title: Media Range and conditional request handling is wrong (bad ranges return 206 full body, If-None-Match ignored, HEAD reads body)
defects.claim: Media serving at links.ts:383-406 passes Range through without validation: `bytes=999999-`, `bytes=garbage`, `bytes=10-5` and multi-range requests return 206 with the whole object instead of 416 or 200 (production R2 may throw instead, surfacing as the generic 500). `If-None-Match` is ignored (always 200), and HEAD downloads the object body (an R2 Class B operation).
defects.scenario: Repro (local R2 emulator): `bytes=999999-`, `bytes=garbage`, `bytes=10-5` and multi-range requests all returned 206 with the whole object.
defects.fix: Parse `Range` yourself; return 416 if `start >= size` and 200 when the range is unparseable; pass `onlyIf: request.headers` and return 304; use `CLIPS.head()` for HEAD.

defects.title: Media is publicly cacheable for up to an hour after deletion, and not marked noindex
defects.claim: links.ts:395 sends `public, max-age=min(left, 3600)` on media, so a deleted, moderated or account-deleted clip stays in browser and intermediary caches for up to an hour, although the page promises it is 'removed immediately'. Media responses have no `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, and `api.clippiboy.com/robots.txt` returns 401.
defects.scenario: A user deletes a clip or their account; browsers and intermediary caches keep serving the media for up to an hour. Media can be indexed by search engines.
defects.fix: `private, max-age=300` or `no-cache` with an ETag, and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on media and on the gone page.

defects.title: Missing CSP, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and no-store headers on share and sign-in pages
defects.claim: The share page (links.ts:372) and the auth pages (index.ts:242) send no Content-Security-Policy, `frame-ancestors` or `Referrer-Policy`. The callback page carries the one-time code but has no `Cache-Control: no-store`. Escaping is correct, so this is defence in depth only.
defects.scenario: If an escaping regression is ever introduced there is no CSP to stop script execution; the pages can be framed; the callback page with the one-time code may be cached.
defects.fix: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'sha256-…'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src https://api.clippiboy.com https://cdn.discordapp.com; media-src https://api.clippiboy.com; font-src https://clippiboy.com; connect-src https://api.clippiboy.com; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `Cache-Control: no-store` on the callback page.

defects.title: Idle sessions are rejected after 180 days but never deleted
defects.claim: Session lifecycle gap: idle sessions are rejected after 180 days but the `sessions` rows are never deleted (no sweep); they are kept until the account is deleted.
defects.scenario: Stale session rows (token hashes linked to user IDs) accumulate indefinitely for inactive users.
defects.fix: Have the cron delete stale sessions.

defects.title: logins rows (user_id + one-time code) are only cleaned up on the next /auth/start
defects.claim: Session lifecycle gap: `logins` rows, which hold `user_id` and the one-time code, are only cleaned up when someone next calls `/auth/start` (the `DELETE FROM logins WHERE created_at < ?` there); there is no cron cleanup.
defects.scenario: With no further sign-in starts, login rows containing user IDs and one-time codes persist indefinitely, including after account deletion.
defects.fix: Have the cron delete stale logins.

defects.title: No 'sign out everywhere'
defects.claim: Session lifecycle gap: there is no way to revoke all of a user's sessions ('sign out everywhere'); only `POST /auth/logout` for the current session exists.
defects.scenario: A user whose token leaked or whose device was lost cannot revoke other sessions.
defects.fix: Add `DELETE /sessions`.

defects.title: Logout and suspension do not close an already-open WebSocket
defects.claim: Session lifecycle gap: the bearer token is only checked when the `/ws` socket connects (index.ts:82-91), so logout and suspension do not close a socket that is already open.
defects.scenario: A user logs out (or is suspended) while connected; their existing WebSocket keeps receiving presence and relays.
defects.fix: Call `closeAll` on logout of the last session or on suspension.

defects.title: Cron uses Promise.all inside waitUntil, so a sweep rejection can cut sweepUsage short
defects.claim: The scheduled handler at index.ts:45 runs `sweep` and `sweepUsage` with `Promise.all` inside `waitUntil`: if `sweep` rejects, the invocation may end while `sweepUsage` is still running.
defects.scenario: An R2 error makes `sweep` reject; the cron invocation ends early and `sweepUsage` does not finish.
defects.fix: Use `Promise.allSettled`.

defects.title: sweep runs its cleanup steps in sequence, so one R2 error skips the rest including the 30-day report deletion
defects.claim: Within `sweep` (links.ts:419-448) the steps run in sequence without per-step error handling, so an R2 error skips the stale-upload cleanup, the tombstone purge, and the 30-day report deletion (a privacy-page promise).
defects.scenario: A transient R2 failure in the expiry step means stale pending uploads, tombstones and old reports are not purged that hour (or repeatedly, if the failure persists).
defects.fix: Wrap each step on its own.

defects.title: Account deletion fails for accounts with more than 500 live links
defects.claim: At links.ts:305 account deletion removes all live shares' R2 objects in one R2 `delete` call. More than 500 live shares means more than 1,000 keys in one call, which throws, so `DELETE /me` returns 500. Only reachable for accounts with `unlimited_links` or `QUICK_LINKS_FOR`.
defects.scenario: An `unlimited_links` account with 501+ live shares calls `DELETE /me` and gets a 500; the account cannot be deleted.
defects.fix: Delete in chunks of 1,000 keys.

defects.title: The MP4 checker has no cap on box count (CPU exhaustion)
defects.claim: The MP4 box checker at shares.ts:173-216 iterates boxes with no limit on how many top-level boxes a file may contain.
defects.scenario: Bench: a 50 MB file made of 6.5M 8-byte boxes takes about 1.1 s of CPU in V8 (a normal file takes 0.2 ms). It passes the check, and on the Free plan it runs past the CPU limit and stalls the isolate.
defects.fix: Refuse files with more than about 100k top-level boxes.

defects.title: Note: MP4/HTML polyglots are accepted; safety relies on fixed video/mp4 type plus nosniff
defects.claim: The MP4 checker accepts an MP4/HTML polyglot (ftyp + moov + size-0 mdat + HTML). This is by design, and it is safe only because media is served with a fixed `video/mp4` type plus `nosniff`.
defects.scenario: Repro: the polyglot was accepted. If the fixed Content-Type or `nosniff` were ever dropped, the upload could be interpreted as HTML.
defects.fix: Keep the fixed `video/mp4` type and `nosniff` (and document the polyglot case in tests).

defects.title: Friend requests: no rate limit or pending cap, and 404 vs 403 responses enable user enumeration
defects.claim: `POST /friends/request` (index.ts:313-345) has no rate limit and no cap on outgoing pending requests, and Discord usernames can be guessed. The response distinguishes 404 (no such user, or they blocked you) from 403 (allow_requests is off), which reveals which Discord accounts use ClippiBoy.
defects.scenario: A script spams friend requests by guessed Discord usernames and uses the 403/404 distinction to learn which Discord accounts use ClippiBoy.
defects.fix: Rate-limit; cap outgoing pending requests at around 20; return the same answer for 403 and 404.

defects.title: Usernames are only synced at login, so two users rows can share a username after a Discord rename
defects.claim: Usernames are only synced at login (db.ts:93-119) and `username` is not unique, so after a Discord rename two rows can share a username.
defects.scenario: User X renames on Discord and user Y takes X's old name; until X logs in again, both rows hold the same username, so a friend request by Discord username can match the wrong account.
defects.fix: Make `username` unique and sync it on use.

defects.title: Posters can be swapped any number of times
defects.claim: `PUT /shares/:id/poster` (links.ts:273-289) lets the owner replace the poster (the `og:image` in Discord and Twitter embeds) with any JPEG, any number of times, with no limit.
defects.scenario: Costs R2 Class A operations and allows bait-and-switch previews: a link is posted with a harmless preview, then the poster is swapped.
defects.fix: Allow one poster PUT per share, or a few at most.

defects.title: Expiry rounding overstates the time left
defects.claim: shares.ts:98 computes the expiry text with `Math.round(left / DAY_MS)`, which rounds up partial days.
defects.scenario: With 12 hours left the page says 'in 1 day'; with 4.5 days left it says 'in 5 days'.
defects.fix: Use `Math.floor` for days, and show hours below 2 days.

defects.title: workers_dev: true lets anyone bypass zone-level WAF and rate-limit rules
defects.claim: The friends Worker has `workers_dev: true`, so it is reachable at its `*.workers.dev` address in addition to `api.clippiboy.com`, which lets anyone bypass zone-level WAF and rate-limit rules.
defects.scenario: An attacker targets the workers.dev address to avoid any WAF or zone rate-limit rule added for api.clippiboy.com.
defects.fix: Turn off `workers_dev`.

defects.title: QUICK_LINKS_FOR is read from env through a cast and missing from secrets.d.ts
defects.claim: `QUICK_LINKS_FOR` reaches `env` through a cast (links.ts:67) and is missing from `secrets.d.ts`.
defects.scenario: Type checking cannot catch a misspelled or missing `QUICK_LINKS_FOR` binding.
defects.fix: Not stated explicitly; implied: declare `QUICK_LINKS_FOR` in `secrets.d.ts` and drop the cast.

defects.title: The site proxy is not covered by npm run check
defects.claim: The site proxy is not type-checked by `npm run check`, because the tsconfig only includes `src`.
defects.scenario: Type errors in site-proxy code ship without being caught by the check script.
defects.fix: Not stated explicitly; implied: include the site proxy in the type check.

defects.title: Site proxy Location rewrite can produce a protocol-relative URL
defects.claim: The site proxy's Location rewrite `location.slice("/clippiboy".length)` (site-proxy/index.ts:41) would turn `/clippiboy//x` into the protocol-relative `//x`.
defects.scenario: An upstream redirect to `/clippiboy//x` is rewritten to `//x`, which the browser resolves as a different host. Speculative.
defects.fix: Only rewrite results that start with a single `/`.

defects.title: Privacy page: suspension promise ('signed out ... links are taken down') is not implemented
defects.claim: The privacy page says: "A suspended account is signed out, cannot sign in or share links, and its links are taken down." Only 'cannot sign in again' and 'cannot create links' are implemented. Existing sessions, sockets, relays, live links and poster swaps keep working, and the ban disappears on `DELETE /me` (same root cause as SV-1).
defects.scenario: Repro: a banned user's session, presence, relays, live links and poster PUT all kept working, and `DELETE /me` removed the ban.
defects.fix: Implement the promise (see SV-1 fix) or change the wording.

defects.title: Privacy page: usage stats called 'anonymous' are actually pseudonymous
defects.claim: The privacy page says usage stats are 'anonymous', with an installation number 'not linked to you'. In practice it is pseudonymous: a persistent installation ID with a per-day profile kept up to 400 days. A unique `/get/<ref>` handed to a single person would identify them.
defects.scenario: An operator hands a unique download ref to one person; their downloads and the resulting installation's daily profile are then attributable to them.
defects.fix: Either commit to never issuing per-person refs, or say 'pseudonymous'.

defects.title: Privacy page: 'does not store your IP address' may be undermined by invocation logs
defects.claim: The privacy page says 'Our server does not store your IP address with it.' That is true for D1, but `observability.enabled` (wrangler.jsonc:8) turns on invocation logs, which may record request metadata (time, path `/t/ping`, possibly IP and headers) for some days.
defects.scenario: Invocation logs retain per-request metadata, possibly including IPs, for `/t/ping` calls. Speculative: check in the dashboard.
defects.fix: Consider turning invocation logs off or excluding `/t/ping`.

defects.title: Privacy page: 'database is located in Western Europe' unverifiable; Hub DO storage not pinned to EU
defects.claim: The privacy page says 'The database is located in Western Europe.' The D1 and R2 locations cannot be verified from the repo. The Hub Durable Object storage (presence, status text, game, last seen) is not pinned to a jurisdiction (no `jurisdiction("eu")`), so it is created wherever the user first connects.
defects.scenario: A user who first connects from outside Europe gets their presence, status, game and last-seen data stored outside Western Europe.
defects.fix: Not stated explicitly; implied: pin the Hub namespace with `jurisdiction("eu")` and verify D1/R2 locations, or adjust the wording.

defects.title: Privacy page: 'No cookies' while api.clippiboy.com sets cb_login
defects.claim: The privacy page says 'No cookies.', but `api.clippiboy.com` sets the `cb_login` cookie during sign-in. It is strictly necessary, so this is a wording issue.
defects.scenario: A reader of the privacy page is told no cookies are set, but the sign-in flow sets one.
defects.fix: Reword the privacy page to mention the strictly necessary sign-in cookie.

defects.title: Privacy page: share links say 'display name and avatar' but also expose the Discord user ID
defects.claim: The privacy page says share links show 'display name and avatar'. The avatar URL also exposes the Discord user ID (same issue as SV-10).
defects.scenario: Anyone with a share link reads the uploader's Discord snowflake ID from the avatar URL.
defects.fix: Proxy or replace the avatar, or disclose it (see SV-10).

defects.title: Privacy page: 'Delete account removes everything immediately' is not fully true
defects.claim: The privacy page says deleting the account removes everything 'immediately'. Media can survive in caches for up to an hour (`public, max-age`); `logins` rows stay until the next sign-in start; reports referencing the share IDs stay 30 days (they hold no personal data).
defects.scenario: After account deletion, clips remain fetchable from caches for up to an hour and login rows remain until someone next starts a sign-in.
defects.fix: Shorten/privatise media caching and sweep logins in the cron (see SV-19, SV-22), or adjust the wording.

defects.title: README: sessions 'expire after 180 days' but rows are kept
defects.claim: The README says sessions 'expire after 180 days'. They are rejected after that, but the rows are kept until the account is deleted.
defects.scenario: Session rows of long-inactive users persist indefinitely despite the documented expiry.
defects.fix: Delete stale sessions in the cron (see SV-21).

defects.title: Spec: 'no public counting route anyone could call' contradicted by /get/<ref>
defects.claim: The spec says there is 'no public counting route anyone could call'. `/get/<ref>` is itself that route, and its counts can be forged freely. The spec accepts fake pings but not fake downloads.
defects.scenario: Anyone with a browser User-Agent inflates download counts for any ref.
defects.fix: Rate-limit or otherwise protect `/get` counting (see SV-4), or update the spec.

defects.title: Missing tests: auth flow (state mismatch, code reuse, expiry, verifier, bans)
defects.claim: Today's 25 tests only cover pure functions. There are no integration tests (e.g. @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers or Miniflare with real D1, R2 and Durable Objects) for the auth flow: cookie/state mismatch, code reuse, expired login, wrong verifier, banned user at callback and on every authenticated route, and `DELETE /me` while banned.
defects.scenario: The suspension bypass (SV-1) and any regression in login CSRF/verifier checks ship undetected.
defects.fix: Add these tests with @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers or Miniflare.

defects.title: Missing tests: authorization matrix
defects.claim: No test covers the authorization matrix: cross-user `DELETE` and poster `PUT` on shares, accept by the requester, and block and friendship interactions.
defects.scenario: A regression in owner or recipient-only checks would not be caught.
defects.fix: Add integration tests for these cases.

defects.title: Missing tests: upload quota race and upload edge cases
defects.claim: No test covers the upload quota race (N parallel uploads), abandoned pending uploads, a body shorter or longer than its Content-Length, or that a non-MP4 gives 415 and leaves no R2 object behind.
defects.scenario: Regressions in the atomic quota INSERT…SELECT or upload cleanup would not be caught.
defects.fix: Add integration tests for these cases.

defects.title: Missing tests: Mp4Boxes edge cases
defects.claim: No test covers `Mp4Boxes` edge cases: size-0 box to the end of the file, 64-bit largesize, size smaller than the header, `ftyp` over 1 KB, very many tiny boxes (CPU), and the documented polyglot case.
defects.scenario: The box-count CPU issue (SV-28) and regressions in box parsing go undetected.
defects.fix: Add unit tests for these cases.

defects.title: Missing tests: share page rendering and response headers
defects.claim: No snapshot test of `renderPage` with hostile title, game, tags and uploader name, plus the response headers (`nosniff`, cache, CSP once added).
defects.scenario: An escaping or header regression on the public share page would not be caught.
defects.fix: Add a snapshot test with hostile inputs and header assertions.

defects.title: Missing tests: Hub behaviour
defects.claim: No test covers the Hub: relay to a non-friend, relay to an invisible friend, relay budget across several sockets, presence fan-out only to accepted friends, the stale-socket alarm, and `closeAll`.
defects.scenario: The per-socket relay budget bypass (SV-6) and invisible-probe leak (SV-7) shipped undetected.
defects.fix: Add Durable Object integration tests for these cases.

defects.title: Missing tests: body limits
defects.claim: No test covers body limits: `handlePing`, report and `body()` with chunked oversized bodies, and with `null` or array JSON.
defects.scenario: The unbounded-body (SV-8) and null-body 500 (SV-15) issues shipped undetected.
defects.fix: Add tests for these cases.

defects.title: Missing tests: sweep
defects.claim: No test covers the sweep: expired, stale-pending and tombstone purge; partial R2 failure; reports past 30 days; the usage cutoff boundary.
defects.scenario: Cron robustness failures (SV-25, SV-26) and retention-promise regressions go undetected.
defects.fix: Add integration tests for the sweep steps.

defects.title: Missing tests: Range and conditional requests
defects.claim: No test covers Range and conditional requests: unsatisfiable, multi-range, suffix ranges, `If-None-Match`, HEAD.
defects.scenario: The incorrect 206-with-full-body behaviour (SV-18) went undetected.
defects.fix: Add tests for these cases.

defects.title: Missing tests: site proxy
defects.claim: No test covers the site proxy: `refFromPath`, HEAD not counted, bots not counted, the Location rewrite, and pinning of `release.setup.url`.
defects.scenario: Regressions in download counting, the Location rewrite (SV-37) or release URL pinning (SV-14) go undetected.
defects.fix: Add tests for these cases.

defects.title: Missing tests: expiresIn boundaries
defects.claim: No test covers `expiresIn` at 12 h, 36 h and 4.5 days.
defects.scenario: The rounding bug that overstates time left (SV-33) went undetected.
defects.fix: Add unit tests at these boundaries.

proposals.title: Integration test harness with real D1, R2 and Durable Objects
proposals.value: Today's 25 tests only cover pure functions; an integration harness would let the auth, authorization, quota, Hub, sweep, body-limit and Range behaviours be tested and keep the security fixes from regressing.
proposals.sketch: Use `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` or Miniflare with real D1, R2 and Durable Object bindings, and add the 11 test areas listed in the report's 'Most valuable missing tests' section.

positives: All SQL uses bound parameters; the only interpolations are constant fragments.
The share quota INSERT…SELECT is atomic and cannot be raced (repro: 6 parallel uploads from one account gave 3x200 and 3x429).

The sign-in flow is sound: the `cb_login` state cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/auth), single-use code (spent on the first try) and S256 verifier check (with `sameText`) together stop both login CSRF and deep-link hijack; the 256-bit bearer token is stored only as a hash.
Owner checks hold (repro: account A deleting B's share gets 403).
Friendship is checked before every relay, and `X-User` is overwritten by the Worker before handing off to the Hub.
Durable Object RPC methods (`card`, `friendPresence`, `relay`, `friendsChanged`, `closeAll`) can only be called from Worker code.
There are no admin or moderation HTTP endpoints, so there is no operator-auth surface to attack.
Share page escaping is correct (repro: `
Media is served with a fixed `video/mp4` or `image/jpeg` type and `nosniff`.

Site proxy: the upstream host (`https://einfabo.github.io/clippiboy`) is fixed, so it is not an open proxy and no SSRF was found; request headers are not forwarded upstream, so there is no header-based cache poisoning; non-GET/HEAD requests get 405.
`putPoster` already bounds its body size (JPEG of at most 1 MB).
`REPORT_LIMIT` rate-limits reports per IP without storing the address; reports are capped at 20 open per share.
MP4 box parsing is otherwise correct: largesize is handled, `size < header` is refused, and a first box other than `ftyp` (or one over 1 KB) is refused.

Consistent with the privacy page: downloads store only `(day, ref, count)` and the proxy has no observability configured; the 400-day retention works (the cutoff keeps 400–401 days); report rows hold no reporter or IP; relays store nothing (`console.error` logs user IDs only on errors); only the `identify` Discord scope is used; tombstones drop title, game and tags and are purged after 2 weeks.
The privacy-page statement that the server does not store the IP address is true for D1.
